page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores via hyperthreading. It provides 16 GB of memory, resulting in a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. The underlying hardware includes a 260 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets, including Intel AVX-512 and AMX matrix math operations. No attached local NVMe storage or discrete GPU hardware is included with this server configuration.

Benchmark results highlight a division between single-threaded and multi-core operations. Single-core tests show moderate execution rates, with average performance scores in Geekbench single-core tests (1807.0) and gzip compression (28.23 GB/sec). Conversely, multi-core and memory-intensive metrics fall in the lower quartile, such as a PassMark CPU score of 6010.98 and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 32.36 GB/sec. Small language model token generation achieves 118.57 tokens per second on a 135M model, whereas database operations and Redis request handling show constrained throughput figures.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance delivers a standard resource density suited for entry-level backend services without requiring local flash storage or dedicated accelerators. While multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth limit its effectiveness for intensive parallel compute or high-scale in-memory caching, it functions adequately for light web serving, basic text processing tasks, microservices, and general-purpose development environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose cloud instance offering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores, paired with 16 GB of RAM. Featuring an instruction set that includes Intel AVX-512 and AMX accelerator extensions alongside a 260 MB L3 cache, the instance operates with no bundled GPU or local NVMe storage. Benchmarks demonstrate solid single-core efficiency, indicated by average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles, as seen in Geekbench multi-core and PassMark memory benchmarks. Achieving 6.53 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, this configuration provides a standard resource density for modest workload demands. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, lightweight web servers, basic API services, and microservice hosting.
